clue.text: Embraces work on relief that's out of order

indicators.note: the relief-working word sits out of, i.e. around, the abbreviation for the order

parts.note: to emboss is to work a design in raised relief
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Someone fumbling an embossing job has their hugs declared improper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' puts EMBOSS outside OM, the Order of Merit, a British honour. 'Out of order' looks like a single anagram signal, but it splits.
explanation.definitionFit: To embosom someone is an old word for clasping them to the breast, a hug.

clue.text: Out of order, please pass by

indicators.note: words out of order are rearranged, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A broken machine sign politely asking passers-by to move on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of order' rearranges the letters of PLEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses passes by.

clue.text: Only a hundred in bud

parts.note: but means only, as in 'but a child'
a ton is slang for a hundred

explanation.surface: Just a hundred flowers in bud.
explanation.walkthrough: A ton is British slang for a hundred (runs, or miles per hour).
explanation.definitionFit: A button is a small unopened flower head or young mushroom, a bud.

clue.text: It takes its turn between washing and ironing

definitions.text: It takes its turn between washing and ironing

parts.words: It takes its turn between washing and ironing
parts.note: a laundry appliance that spins, taking its turn after the wash and before the iron

explanation.surface: Something waiting in line during laundry day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' means spin: the machine whirls clothes to dry them.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin-drier is a machine that removes water from laundry by rotating it fast.

clue.text: 14 ac for instance — just the chap for the post

definitions.meaning: 14 across is a novelist, an example of a writer by trade

definitions.text: just the chap for the post
definitions.meaning: read literally, a fellow carrying mail, which is a postman's job

explanation.surface: A writer would suit the job, it says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like a job vacancy but means the mail: a man of letters, read literally, is a postman.
explanation.definitionFit: A man of letters is a scholar or author; read literally, a man with a sack of mail.

clue.text: To wit, birds saying it get angry looks

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation of scilicet, Latin for 'namely' or 'to wit'
owls are the birds traditionally heard calling 'to-wit, to-woo', so they say 'to wit'

explanation.surface: Birds hooting their call are met with glares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to 'To wit', the owl's call, so the phrase does double service in the picture though only once in the parse.
explanation.definitionFit: Scowls are frowning glares of displeasure.

clue.text: " Stretch ' or " bird "

definitions.meaning: to stretch one's neck to see
a tall wading bird with a long neck

explanation.definitionFit: To crane is to stretch the neck; the crane is also a long-legged wading bird.

clue.text: Promise amusement with a pun

parts.note: to give one's word is to promise
play is amusement or fun

explanation.surface: A vow of fun with a joke attached.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end, 'with' linking the pieces to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun is a joke playing on a word's double meaning.

clue.text: Thus enlightened, due to rebuild the Ivory tower

parts.note: so means thus
lit means illuminated

indicators.note: rebuilding means the letters of the word due are put together anew

explanation.surface: An enlightened scholar reconstructing his ivory tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rebuild' rearranges DUE into UDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ivory tower is a place of seclusion apart from the world, a state of being alone.

clue.text: Pismires pride ? — downfall, rather

parts.note: pismires are ants, so a pride of their own big cats would be lions of the ants; but the insect so named preys on ants, being their downfall rather than their pride

explanation.surface: Ants' pride, or rather their fall.
explanation.walkthrough: PISMIRE is an old word for ant; a pride is a group of lions. The ant-lion larva traps ants in a sand pit.
explanation.definitionFit: The ant-lion is an insect whose larva digs pits to catch ants.

clue.text: Is one helpless over this kind of organ ?

definitions.text: Is one helpless over this kind of organ ?

parts.words: Is one helpless over this kind of organ ?
parts.note: to be 'over a' certain container is to be helpless; the same container names a hand-cranked street organ

explanation.surface: A question about feeling powerless before some musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over a barrel' is an idiom for being at someone's mercy; a barrel organ is the hand-turned instrument of street musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A cask is the container that both the helplessness idiom and the street organ are named after.

clue.text: Idle ? Definitely not

definitions.meaning: idle means inactive, not doing anything
a firm refusal, an idiom for 'no way'

explanation.definitionFit: Being idle is doing nothing; 'nothing doing' is a colloquial flat refusal.

clue.text: Every puny whipster got Othello's

parts.note: a quotation from Othello's last scene, where the Moor laments that every puny whipster gets his blade

explanation.surface: Any feeble youngster took the Moor's possession.
explanation.walkthrough: In Othello Act 5, Othello says 'I am not valiant neither, But every puny whipster gets my sword.'
explanation.definitionFit: Othello's weapon, the blade he says any weakling can now take from him.

clue.text: Best to have a lot of money — it holds the root of growth

definitions.text: it holds the root of growth

parts.note: the flower of something is its finest part
a pot is a large sum, as in 'pots of money'

explanation.surface: Advice that wealth is the best thing, plus a remark about what feeds growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'root of growth' is literal: the definition is a container in which a plant's roots grow.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant container filled with soil, in which the roots of a growing plant sit.

clue.text: Jockey, drawn by an author

parts.note: a jockey is one who rides horses
drawn means looking gaunt and worn out

explanation.surface: A jockey sketched by some writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn' looks like a sketch, but it means gaunt-faced. H. Rider Haggard wrote King Solomon's Mines.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Rider Haggard was a Victorian novelist, writer of adventure stories such as She.

clue.text: Defiant things, once they're off your hands

definitions.text: Defiant things, once they're off your hands

parts.words: Defiant things, once they're off your hands
parts.note: armoured gloves which, thrown down, issued a challenge

explanation.surface: Rebellious objects you are glad to be rid of.
explanation.walkthrough: Throwing down the gauntlet was the knight's challenge: the gloves become defiant once off the hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauntlets are armoured gloves, whose throwing down was a sign of challenge.

clue.text: More whimsical point for connoisseurs

parts.note: fancy means whimsical, so fancier is more whimsical
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A more whimsical point for experts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Fanciers are enthusiasts with a keen eye, such as pigeon or dog fanciers.

clue.text: Tie one lady in knots — what could be better?

indicators.note: tied in knots means tangled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Tying a lady up in knots, and nothing better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in knots' rearranges TIE, I (one) and LADY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideality is the quality of being ideal, perfection that cannot be bettered.

clue.text: The language of summer in a.fern

parts.note: read as 'one who sums', an adder
a tongue is a language

explanation.surface: Asking what the language of the warm season might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is not the season but one who does sums, an adder; the tongue of an adder gives the plant name.
explanation.definitionFit: Adder's-tongue is a small fern whose spore spike resembles a snake's tongue.

clue.text: It needs peeling perhaps or darning

definitions.text: It needs peeling perhaps or darning

parts.words: It needs peeling perhaps or darning
parts.note: a vegetable often peeled, and also the slang for a hole in a sock that wants mending

explanation.surface: Household chores: something to peel or sew.
explanation.walkthrough: A potato is British slang for a hole in a sock or stocking, through which the heel shows.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuber that is peeled before cooking, and the sock hole needing a darn.

clue.text: Confine one northern bird …

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Caging a seabird from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opening verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern is to detain or imprison, especially in wartime.

clue.text: Privileged three-card trick

indicators.note: a trick here is a sleight that shuffles the letters of the words into a new order

explanation.surface: A card-sharp's game earning special licence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trick' rearranges the nine letters of THREECARD. The three-card trick is the street con also called find the lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A chartered body holds rights by royal charter, so it is privileged.

clue.text: … another bird, an enormous one

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Following on, a second bird, a huge one.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link to 20 down's bird; 'another' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A Titan is a giant, from the gigantic gods of Greek myth.

clue.text: What Browning's snail was on

parts.note: Robert Browning's Pippa Passes says the snail is on a prickly branch: 'The snail's on the ...'

explanation.surface: A literary question about a poem's gastropod.
explanation.walkthrough: From Pippa's song: 'The lark's on the wing; The snail's on the thorn; God's in his heaven, All's right with the world!'
explanation.definitionFit: The prickly spike in Pippa's song where the poet places his snail.

clue.text: Is second, among the way-out facilities provided

indicators.note: the abbreviation for second is placed among the letters of the doors word

parts.note: exits are ways out

explanation.surface: Someone is second among the outlandish amenities on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way-out' suggests eccentric, but it means ways out, exits; 'among' puts S inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is simply to be, so the verb for being.

clue.text: Trotted out to get a drink, the dog!

parts.note: to trot out an opinion is to air it
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A dog paraded at a show is rewarded with a beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trotted out' suggests a dog being walked, but it means aired, as of views.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier breed from Yorkshire.

clue.text: The patent goes without it

parts.note: patent means obvious, and what is obvious, as the idiom has it, goes without a certain word

explanation.surface: A legal remark that a patent lacks something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patent' looks legal but means obvious: it goes without saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverb or expression is what the obvious need not have, as the idiom says.

clue.text: It brought excellent parts to a curate

definitions.text: It brought excellent parts to a curate

parts.words: It brought excellent parts to a curate
parts.note: the curate's breakfast was good in parts, and this utensil served it to him

explanation.surface: A tool that carried fine pieces to a junior clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: A Punch cartoon has a curate served a bad egg say it is 'good in parts', hence a curate's egg. The utensil served it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spoon for eating a boiled egg, the kind the curate would have used.
